claims.text: There is a significant positive heat of mixing between refractory alloying elements and Cu.
Ab initio molecular dynamics simulations can predict the thermodynamic stability of RHEA-Cu alloys.
Ab initio molecular dynamics simulations can be used to optimize the composition of RHEA-Cu alloys.
Simulation-based composition optimization can guide the selection of suitable alloying elements and compositions.
Simulation-based composition optimization will result in a stable RHEA-Cu microstructure at high temperature.
Simulation-based composition optimization will enable a large-scale reaction at high temperature.
The resulting microstructure will have a grain size of at least 10 μm at 1000°C.
The resulting reaction rate will be at least 90% at 1000°C.
Commonly used composite-forming methods produce a grain size of approximately 5 μm at 1000°C.
Commonly used composite-forming methods produce a reaction rate of approximately 50% at 1000°C.
The simulations are applicable only above 800°C.
The simulations are limited to reactions having reaction rates above 50%.
Simulation accuracy may be affected by alloy-composition complexity and computational-method limitations.
Experimental validation of the simulated results may be challenging.

contradictions.description: The stated domain is restricted to reaction rates above 50%, but the falsification rule applies to any rate below 80%, including values outside that declared domain.
